question.text: The Ming dynasty was established after the Red Turban rebellions that overthrew this Chinese successor dynasty to the Mongol Empire. Marco Polo's writings about China were during the time of this dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Yuan Dynasty [do not accept or prompt on "Mongol Dynasty"]
question.clue: It ended when the Red Turban Rebellion forced Togon Temur to flee its capital of Dadu in 1368.

swap.text: This is the total number of women who have ever been Supreme Court justices, past and present.
swap.clue: Jiang Qing, Mao's final wife, was a member of a group of this number of people. Sparrows were exterminated as part of a campaign against this number of pests.

question.text: The UK turned over control of this Special Administrative Region to China in 1997, two years beforePortugal did the same with nearby Macau.
question.clue: A series of protests in this city was named after the umbrellas used to shield demonstrators from police tear gas.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese history.
swap.text: This rebellion's leader, Hong Xiuquan, claimed to be the brother of Jesus, and it attempted to establish a "Heavenly Kingdom" in mid-nineteenth century China.
swap.clue: This rebellion began among the Hakka people, and it at first advocated the segregation of men and women and the abolishment of private property.

question.text: Japanese leader Toyotomi Hideyoshi invaded Joseon as a stepping stone to attacking this Chinese dynasty. This dynasty was founded by the Hongwu ["hohng-woo"] Emperor after he won the Battle of Lake Poyang ["p'woh-yong"].
question.clue: Under this dynasty's Yongle emperor, seven voyages by the mariner Zheng He explored the Indian Ocean.

swap.leadin: This man purged communist members of his army in the 1926 Canton Coup.
swap.text: Name this Chinese leader and protege of Sun Yat-Sen. His kidnapping in the Xi'an Incident led to a united Chinese front against the Japanese in World War Two.
swap.clue: Over 3,000 critics were executed as a result of martial law imposed by this leader in an event known as the White Terror.

question.text: The Silla Kingdom allied with this Chinese dynasty to conquer its neighbors. This dynasty was interrupted by Wu Zetian's short-lived Zhou Dynasty.
question.clue: This dynasty lost the battle of Talas to the Abbasids.

swap.leadin: During this campaign, an inconsequential skirmish at the Luding Bridge somehow became a major propaganda victory for one side.
swap.text: Name this arduous retreat undertaken from 1934 to 1935 by the Chinese Communist Party after the Jiangxi Soviet was surrounded by Nationalist forces.
swap.clue: The Fifth Encirclement forced this event, which Otto Braun took part in. The participants of this event defeated warlord forces at the Battle of Luding Bridge and reshuffled their leadership at the Zunyi Conference.

question.leadin: This founder of the state of Wei rose to prominence in the wake of Dong Zhuo's tyranny by defeating Yuan Shao at the Battle of Guandu.
question.text: Identify this Machiavellian strategist from Chinese history, who was ultimately defeated by Liu Bei at the Battle of Red Cliffs and died after Hua Tuo tried to combine cannabis and neural surgery.
question.clue: This man's campaign to restore the lands of the Eastern Han was halted at the Battle of Red Cliffs, where he was defeated by Liu Bei and Sun Quan ].

swap.leadin: The discovery of these objects provided archaeological evidence for Sima Qian's ("suh-mah ch'YEN's") account of early Chinese history in Records of the Grand Historian.
swap.text: Give this two-word English term, or the Chinese equivalent, for objects like ox scapulae that were heated until they cracked in a form of divination from the Shang dynasty.
swap.clue: The so-called "Waste of Yin" was an important site for the collection of these items, which sometimes bore messages about toothache, the success of deer-hunting, or appropriate dates for the birth of a child.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the United States' involvement in China during World War II.
question.text: Claire Lee Chennault led the American Volunteer Group, a volunteer air force in China during World War II that is usually referred to by this two-word English nickname.
question.clue: The plan to create this group was put forth by its leader's press officer Joseph Alsop, and approved after a lengthy debate at the Trident Conference, to the dismay of a man known as "Vinegar Joe," Joseph Stilwell.

swap.text: This period during the Zhou Dynasty lasted from about 771 to 476 BC. Its name came from a history by Confucius. During this period, feudalism declined and larger states became more powerful, leading to violence that would be seen in the later Warring States period.
swap.answerHtml: Spring and Autumn Period [accept Chun qiu shi dai]
swap.clue: That royal family's flight from Zongzhou to Chengzhou initiated this time period, which the rise of the states of Wu and Yue.

question.text: Along with the Treaty of Aigun, a pair of treaties by this name ended the Second Opium War. It ordered China to pay reparations to the British and French, and directly to British merchants for destruction of their property

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Chinese dynasty.
swap.text: This dynasty, whose name translates as pure, survived the Boxer and Taiping Rebellions.

question.text: Mitsuomi Kamio was ordered to take this Chinese city from German control following the entry of Japan in WWI. The siege of this city laid the groundwork for the Japanese expanding their influence in China.
question.clue: During World War I, Japan captured this city in Germany's Kiautschou Bay Concession. This Chinese city is home to St. Michael's Cathedral, built by German missionaries.

swap.leadin: Southern participants in this rebellion were led by Chen Youliang, who established a state he called Great Han.
swap.text: Name this rebellion, which was led by the man who would become the Hongwu Emperor, Zhu Yuanzhang. It took its name from its participants' trademark headwear.
swap.clue: After its completion in 1368, this event brought about the Ming Dynasty.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the defense of Sihang Warehouse.
question.text: The defense of Sihang Warehouse was part of this larger 1937 battle. Nationalist Chinese and invading Japanese armies clashed for over three months in this battle, which decimated China's officer corps and produced a photograph of a baby in a bombed-out railway station titled Bloody Saturday.
question.clue: Including fighting in Luodian and Dachang, this three month long series of battles over a namesake city saw the Chinese under Chiang Kai-shek lose about a quarter of a million troops while using urban warfare strategies and handguns.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about tensions in the lead-up to the Tiananmen Square protests.
swap.text: Student anger was partially directed at these people, the children of senior CCP members who inherited great power. Xi Jinping is an example of these people.

question.leadin: Ai Weiwei created 3,200 porcelain replicas of these animals to protest the demolition of his Shanghai studio.
question.text: Name these animals used to mock Hu Jintao's "Harmonious Society" since they sound like "harmony" in Chinese. The mythical Grass Mud Horse, or Caonima, battles these animals, which are sold live in vending machines in Chinese metro stations in autumn.
question.answerHtml: river crabs [or héxiè; accept other names such as hairy crabs; or mitten crabs; prompt on crustaceans or arthropods or other non-specific answers]

swap.leadin: This format was invented by Wang Anshi, and first appeared around 1465.
swap.text: Name this specific form of "essay" that was required in order to pass the imperial examinations during the later Ming and Qing dynasties. Its rigid structure featured an opening, amplification, and then several arguments.
swap.clue: Imperial exam-takers wrote using this rigid essay format, which included a set number of sections and many formalized parallel sentences.
